hints: Look for the big jump in each row, that is where an electron starts being removed from a much closer, inner shell.
For element X the jump is between the 5th (6274) and 6th (21269) values, so 5 electrons come off relatively easily.
Count the easy electrons to get the Group number, then match that to Period 3 to name X, Y and Z in order.
walkthrough:
**Recall what a big jump means**

Think simply. Electrons in the same outer shell come off with fairly similar energies. When you start on the next inner shell, much closer to the nucleus, the energy shoots up.

Rule to use:
$$\text{number of easy ionisations before the jump = number of outer shell electrons = Group number}$$

**Find the jump for element X**

Look at X: 5th = 6274, 6th = 21269. That is more than a 3 times increase.

After that, 6th to 10th rise only gradually. So 5 electrons are outer electrons. That means Group 15. In Period 3, Group 15 is $\text{P}$.

**Find the jump for element Y**

Look at Y: 5th = 7012, 6th = 8496, then 7th = 27107. The big jump is between 6th and 7th.

So 6 electrons are removed easily. That means Group 16. In Period 3, Group 16 is $\text{S}$.

**Find the jump for element Z and conclude**

Look at Z: 5th = 6542, 6th = 9362, 7th = 11018, then 8th = 33606. The big jump is between 7th and 8th.

So 7 electrons are removed easily. That means Group 17. In Period 3, Group 17 is $\text{Cl}$. Together X, Y, Z are P, S, Cl.

options.A: Na, Mg, Al are Groups 1, 2, 3. They would show big jumps after the 1st, 2nd and 3rd ionisations. Here the jumps are after the 5th, 6th and 7th, so far too late for these metals.
options.B: Mg, Al, Si are Groups 2, 3, 4. They would show jumps after the 2nd, 3rd and 4th ionisations. The data shows 5, 6 and 7 easy electrons, so this undercounts by three in each case.
options.C: P has 5 outer electrons with a jump 5th to 6th, S has 6 outer electrons with a jump 6th to 7th, and Cl has 7 outer electrons with a jump 7th to 8th. This matches the table exactly for X, Y and Z.
options.D: S, Cl, Ar are Groups 16, 17, 18 and would jump after the 6th, 7th and 8th ionisations. X jumps after the 5th, not the 6th, so the whole set is shifted one Group too high.
